summary:
Our team developed TecXust – Space Mission Design Game, an interactive educational game that introduces students to the process of designing and planning a space mission.

The project focuses on the challenges involved in real-world space mission planning, such as selecting mission objectives, designing spacecraft, choosing scientific instruments and launch vehicles, and managing limitations related to budget, power, mass, communication, and orbital constraints.

Our game addresses the challenge by transforming complex engineering concepts into an interactive learning experience. It allows users to explore mission-planning decisions and understand how different requirements and limitations influence a mission.

The main benefit of our project is that it makes space science and engineering more engaging and accessible to students. It encourages critical thinking, problem-solving, creativity, and decision-making while developing an understanding of the challenges involved in space exploration.

Through TecXust, our aim is to inspire students to explore space technology and learn engineering concepts beyond traditional classroom methods.
details:
What does the project do and how does it work?

We developed an interactive Space Mission Design Game that allows users to experience the process of planning a complete space mission. Players explore different mission-planning decisions, including mission objectives, spacecraft design, scientific instruments, launch vehicles, budget, power, mass, communication, and orbital constraints. The project is available as a web-based game.

What are its benefits?

The game makes complex space engineering concepts easier to understand through interactive learning. It encourages critical thinking, problem-solving, decision-making, and an understanding of resource limitations.

What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to make space mission planning more accessible and interesting to students. We want to encourage curiosity about space exploration and introduce students to the engineering decisions involved in planning space missions.

What technologies were used?

  • Web-based application development.
  • Node.js (version 20 or above) and npm for the development environment.
  • Web browser for running the game.
  • No additional hardware is required.

How is the project creative?

Our creativity lies in transforming the complex process of space mission planning into an interactive game. Instead of learning only through textbooks, users can explore mission design through gameplay and decision-making.

What factors did our team consider?

We considered mission objectives, spacecraft design, scientific instruments, launch vehicles, budget limitations, power requirements, mass constraints, communication systems, and orbital requirements. We also considered usability, accessibility, and making the learning experience engaging for students.
